q: 1. The ISO A0 size of drawing is defined as having an area of .............
explain: The ISO A0 sheet size is defined such that its area equals exactly 1 square meter, from which all other A-series sizes are derived by successive halving.

q: 2. The paper size of A4 is .............
explain: The standard ISO A4 paper size is 210 mm × 297 mm, the most commonly used sheet size for general documents and smaller drawings.

q: 3. The title block is provided in a drawing sheet at .............
explain: As per standard drawing sheet layout conventions, the title block is placed in the bottom right-hand corner of the sheet for easy identification when the sheet is folded or filed.

q: 4. Title block in drawing sheets gives the information about .............
explain: The title block consolidates key reference information — drawing title, scale, drawing number, and other details — making 'all of these' the correct comprehensive answer.

q: 5. The size of drawing board required for A0 sheet size in mm is .............
explain: To accommodate an A0 sheet (841×1189 mm) with margins for pinning and T-square movement, a larger drawing board of approximately 1500×1000×25 mm is required.
